transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-11-18 15:00 PST | Duration: 55m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Jenna (CSM), Sara, Eric, Liam (Lumina)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. this is the Lumina onboarding kickoff, really excited to get started. quick intros?
[00:10] Sara: yeah hi, Sara Boyd, head of AI ops at Lumina, i'll be the main contact for infra and security.
[00:16] Eric: eric huang, cto, i'll be involved on architecture decisions esp around private deploys.
[00:23] Liam: liam, platform, i'll work with your se on the vpc peering and k8s stuff.
[00:28] Maya: great, i'll hand off to carlos for a quick run of the onboarding flow then we'll cover questions.
[00:35] Carlos: cool. so high level, onboarding has three phases: provision -> pilot -> scale. provision includes network setup (vpc peering or private endpoint), sso/saml, and key management. pilot is we run a 2 week pilot with your sample prompts to validate latency, cost and quality. scale is dedicated capacity or private deployment depending on needs.
[01:02] Sara: quick Q — we need SOC 2 and audit logs, and also our data residency constraints; are those covered in private? i.e. can we keep everything in our vpc?
[01:12] Carlos: yes, with Redwood Private you can keep the control plane in your VPC or on-prem depending on the package. audit logs, KMS/HSM integrations are supported; i'll attach the security pack in the follow up. small note — sometimes the doc says Redwood inferance instead of inference, sorry the auto text is weird.
[01:32] Eric: when you say "dedicated capacity" what's the typical latency profile? we care about p95 under 200ms for our interactive agent.
[01:41] Carlos: for dedicated reserved pools on A100/Tr4 variants we typically hit p95 ~120-180ms for short-turn tasks with optimized batching disabled. tradeoffs — more batching lowers cost but could add tail latency, and kv cache helps for repeated prefixes. we'll need to run bench—, bench tests on your prompt shapes.
[02:05] Liam: what's the effort to try hosted first then move to dedicated? we prefer to avoid big infra lift initially.
[02:11] Maya: you can start on hosted to iterate, then we do a controlled migration to Dedicated; routing and model pinning helps so your app sees consistent endpoints. Carlos: we also support canary rollouts so you can validate before cutover.
[02:27] Sara: for security review, we need SAML SSO, RBAC, and long-term retention controls — retention must be configurable per env for compliance.
[02:36] Carlos: yep, SAML is standard, RBAC available in the console, retention and audit controls are in the security pack. i'll send the SOC2 summary and the retention page.
[02:46] Jenna: we'll also need the list of Lumina users who need admin vs dev access; can you send that after the meeting?
[02:52] Sara: yes, we'll share that.
[02:55] Carlos: on networking, two paths: vpc peering (lighter lift) or private VPC endpoints. peering requires route table updates and security group rules; endpoints require private DNS configs. liam, which do you prefer?
[03:12] Liam: peering sounds easier for us since we're already peering with cloud partners, but want the endpoints option if we go air-gapped later.
[03:20] Carlos: understood. i'll include both sets of instructions. also note — if you want on-prem, we have an on-prem package but that adds setup time and dedicated ops.
[03:33] Eric: curious about monitoring and cost visibility — can we see per-route token cost and per-request latency?
[03:39] Maya: yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level cost, per-model dashboards, traces, and you can also export logs to your splunk or datadog.
[03:46] Sara: perfect. and for KMS — we use GCP KMS in us-east. supported?
[03:51] Carlos: yes, we support GCP KMS and AWS KMS/HSM integrations; we'll need a key ARN and a service account setup.
[03:59] Sara: ok. regarding pilot success criteria: we want p95 < 200ms, token cost under $0.01 per 1k tokens (rough target), and no data leaving our VPC. is that reasonable?
[04:16] Carlos: those are fair targets; token cost will vary by model and quantization. for cost we can propose quantized variants and batching strategies during pilot.
[04:26] Maya: let's capture metrics: latency, cost per 1k tokens, correctness on sample eval set — we should agree on an eval script.
[04:34] Liam: we'll provide a 2000-example eval set and a sampling of production prompts.
[04:39] Jenna: great, i'll get a tracker ticket for pilot and invite folks.
[04:44] Maya: timeline suggestion: setup network and SSO in week 1, run pilot weeks 2-3, review week 4. any blockers?
[04:53] Sara: need security team sign-off but that should be fine if you share SOC2 and the KMS steps.
[04:58] Eric: also db anonymization — some logs we share must be scrubbed; can we scoping that?
[05:04] Carlos: yes we can redact logs before export and we have configurable logging levels; we'll detail that.
[05:12] Maya: ok next steps recap: i'll send onboarding deck and pricing, carlos will send security pack and network checklist, jenna will create the onboarding project, lumina will share pilot dataset and user access list.
[05:25] Sara: sounds good. can we schedule a technical deep dive with infra and security next week?
[05:30] Carlos: absolutely — i'll propose two times for a technical deep dive (vpc peering, endpoint config, KMS, and benchmark runbook).
[05:37] Maya: thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with links to docs.
[05:40] Eric: thanks.

End of call.

Notes: transcription contains minor auto-caption errors (names sometimes misattributed, product spelled "inferance" once). Shared artifacts referenced: onboarding deck (link to be sent), SOC2 summary (link to be sent), infra checklist (link), pilot eval template (link).
